patterns:
Java ELEMENT_QUERY (java.rs lines 4-13, verbatim): '(method_declaration
  name: (identifier) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (identifier) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration

Java DEFUSE_QUERY (java.rs lines 32-37, verbatim): '(local_variable_declaration declarator: (variable_declarator name: (identifier) @write.local))
(assignment_expression left: (identifier) @write.assign)
(update_expression (identifier) @writeread.update)
(identifier) @read.usage'

Java extract_inheritance (java.rs 131-161) reads child_by_field_name('superclass') and child_by_field_name('interfaces') and emits 'extends X' and 'implements X'; PHP has no such fields, so the same output contract needs an unfielded-children walk.

Swift extract_inheritance (swift.rs 49-75) walks node.child(i) for kind 'inheritance_specifier' and emits 'extends' for the first and 'conforms' for later entries; PHP output uses 'implements' for interfaces, so only the walk style transfers.

approaches.name: A. Full Java-style integration (recommended)
approaches.description: New languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class/interface/trait/enum declarations), CALL_QUERY (function_call_expression, member_call_expression, nullsafe_member_call_expression, scoped_call_expression), REFERENCE_QUERY (named_type), IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_declaration), DEFUSE_QUERY (simple_parameter, assignment_expression, augmented_assignment_expression, update_expression, variable_name), and extract_inheritance that walks the unfielded base_clause and class_interface_clause children. Wire 'php' into get_language_info (defuse Some, extract_inheritance Some, function-name and receiver handlers None as the issue excludes them), get_ts_language with LANGUAGE_PHP, EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages, and README. Inline tests modelled on java.rs and swift.rs plus one integration test file.
pros: Meets every acceptance criterion in issue #1864 including the five queries and DEFUSE_QUERY
Mirrors the Java/Swift contract so downstream analyze_file, analyze_module and def-use paths need no changes
Field-walk is grounded in grammar.json, so the inheritance output is deterministic
cons: Node kinds were verified against node-types.json only; the query text still needs a compile test before wiring
Java's inheritance handler uses field names that PHP lacks, so it cannot be copied verbatim
Requires LANGUAGE_PHP (not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY) to satisfy the HTML-template criterion, which adds the HTML text nodes to the tree

approaches.name: B. Registry-only minimal (DEFUSE_QUERY = None)
approaches.description: Same php.rs but with ELEMENT, CALL, IMPORT and extract_inheritance only, defuse_query None in get_language_info, following the Fortran and CSS precedent (fortran defuse_query: None, css defuse_query: None in mod.rs).
pros: Smallest change and the least grammar-risk surface
Fewer query constants to keep correct across grammar updates
cons: Violates the issue scope, which lists DEFUSE_QUERY as one of the five required constants

With defuse_query None, extract_def_use returns an empty Vec (parser_elements.rs line 850-852 'let Some(defuse_query) = &compiled.defuse else { return vec![] }'), so def-use results for PHP would silently be empty
Leaves the Java/Swift parity gap that the issue explicitly asks to close

approaches.name: C. Derive queries from upstream queries/tags.scm
approaches.description: Start from the grammar's own queries/tags.scm (definition.function, definition.method, definition.class, definition.interface, definition.trait, reference.call, reference.implementation, reference.class) and rename captures to the names parser_elements.rs reads (func_name/method_name, class_name, call, import_path).
pros: Upstream-maintained patterns, so grammar changes are easier to track
Covers object_creation_expression constructors and property declarations, which the issue leaves out of scope
cons: tags.scm has no enum_declaration pattern (verified: its patterns cover namespace, interface, trait, class, method, function, property, object_creation, function_call, scoped_call and member_call only), so enums need a hand-written pattern anyway
tags.scm has no namespace_use_declaration import pattern, so IMPORT_QUERY must still be hand-written
Adds constructor and property captures the issue marks as not in scope, enlarging the output surface

recommendation: Approach A (full Java-style integration). It is the only option that satisfies the issue's five-query and DEFUSE_QUERY scope, and it reuses the registry pattern of Swift and CSS unchanged. Build the queries first and prove them with compile tests (as swift.rs line 97 does) before touching the registry. Use LANGUAGE_PHP so the HTML-template criterion passes. Implement extract_inheritance as an unfielded-children walk over base_clause and class_interface_clause, because PHP exposes no superclass or interfaces fields. Leave the three name-resolution handlers as None per scope. Note the external-PR restriction in the issue before any code work.

inheritance_walk_citation: Grammar source: tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php, php/src/grammar.json and php/src/node-types.json at master (crate tree-sitter-php 0.25.2). class_declaration in grammar.json is a SEQ of: optional FIELD attributes; REPEAT of _modifier; the keyword class; FIELD name (RESERVED name); CHOICE of base_clause or BLANK (NO field name); CHOICE of class_interface_clause or BLANK (NO field name); FIELD body = declaration_list. node-types.json class_declaration: fields {attributes, body, name}; children types [abstract_modifier, base_clause, class_interface_clause, final_modifier, readonly_modifier, static_modifier, var_modifier, visibility_modifier]. base_clause (grammar.json) = SEQ[ALIAS 'extends', SEQ[_name, REPEAT(',' _name)]]; class_interface_clause = SEQ[ALIAS 'implements', SEQ[_name, REPEAT(',' _name)]]. node-types.json base_clause and class_interface_clause have no fields; their children are [name, qualified_name, relative_name]. FIELD-WALK: (1) take class_declaration.child_by_field_name('name') for the class name (unchanged from Java). (2) Do NOT use child_by_field_name('superclass') or ('interfaces'): class_declaration has no such fields (Java's handler uses them). (3) Iterate node.children(&mut cursor) (unfielded children), and for each child with kind 'base_clause' iterate its named children (name | qualified_name | relative_name) and push format!('extends {text}') per name. (4) For each child with kind 'class_interface_clause' iterate its named children and push format!('implements {text}') per name. (5) Skip primitive_type (enum backing type, e.g. enum Suit: string) and attribute_list/modifier children. Consequence: class Foo extends Bar implements A, B yields ["extends Bar", "implements A", "implements B"]; interface I extends A, B yields two 'extends' entries from one base_clause; enum E: string implements I yields ["implements I"]; a class with neither clause yields [].
